newsitem.title: USA: Calif. state Assembly elects Democratic Speaker.
newsitem.headline: Calif. state Assembly elects Democratic Speaker.

text.p: The California state Assembly on Monday elected Democrat Cruz Bustamante as its new Speaker.
Bustamante, a 43-year-old from Fresno, Calif., was elected on a straight party-line vote of 43-to-37, replacing Republican Speaker Curt Pringle.
The vote was taken after Assembly members were sworn in for the new legislative session.
After his election as the 61st Assembly speaker, Bustamante said he would aim to run the state without raising taxes.
"I'd like to see every kid in the state attend college ... I would like to see us teach every second grader to read," he added. "My friends, I challenge the House to do good."
"I think it's pretty obvious that I'm a very happy man today," he said.
Bustamante named Assemblywoman Sheila Kuehl as Assembly Speaker Pro-Temp. Kuehl, a Democrat from Santa Monica, will be the first woman to hold that post.
Also on Monday, the state Senate reelected Senator Bill Lockyer, a Democrat from Hayward, as its President Pro Tem.
In the November election, Democrats regained control of the 80-member Assembly and strengthened their hold on the state Senate.
